newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock funds flow $17.42 bln in Sept - ICI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock funds flow $17.42 bln in Sept - ICI.

text.p: Net new cash flow into stock mutual funds totalled $17.42 billion in September versus $17.92 in August, a mutual fund trade group said Monday.
That figure was in line with the Investment Company Institute's Oct. 9 estimate of a $16 billion flow into stock funds for September.
Net new cash flow into the entire mutual fund industry was $7.32 billion in September, compared with $30.17 billion in the previous month, the ICI said.
Bond and income funds accounted for $1.93 billion of net new cash flow in September, compared with an outflow of $41.5 million in August.
Money market funds had an outflow of $12.04 billion in September, compared with an inflow of $12.29 billion in August, the ICI said.
Net new cash flow is a common measure of demand for shares of mutual funds.
ICI chief economist John Rea noted that September's stock fund inflow, although high by historical standards, represented a moderating of inflows in place since June.
Rea also said that through the first nine months of the year, inflows as a percentage of stock fund assets were lower than those in 1993, the previous record year for inflows.
